quiz.q: Why did Bal Gangadhar Tilak describe constitutional methods before an alien bureaucracy as 'political suicide'?
options: Because constitutional agitation was futile before an alien bureaucracy lacking genuine constitutional governance.
Because direct mass action required immense preparation and subjective consciousness among the unorganized masses.
Because legislative memorials and prayers were addressed only to British rulers rather than Indians.
Because peaceful dialogue inevitably provoked uncontrollable violent peasant uprisings against the rural landholders.
quiz.why: Tilak argued that constitutional methods were meaningless in India because an alien colonial bureaucracy offered no real constitutional governance.

quiz.q: According to Bipin Chandra, why did Mahatma Gandhi alternate active mass struggle with constructive truce periods?
options: To allow the colonial government time to enact promised constitutional reforms peacefully and gradually.
To respect the limited capacity of the masses for sustained sacrifice and prevent exhaustion.
To negotiate secret political compromises with British authorities away from public scrutiny and debate.
To permanently transition the national freedom movement from mass agitational politics to parliamentary elections.
quiz.why: Gandhi understood that ordinary masses have limited endurance, so truce phases allowed people to recuperate through constructive work before resuming struggle.

quiz.q: How did the strategic character of the Civil Disobedience Movement differ fundamentally from Non-Cooperation?
options: Non-Cooperation openly defied statutory laws, whereas Civil Disobedience focused strictly on economic boycotts.
Non-Cooperation was an armed revolt, while Civil Disobedience relied solely on assembly resolutions.
Non-Cooperation passively withheld cooperation, whereas Civil Disobedience actively and deliberately violated colonial laws.
Non-Cooperation demanded complete sovereign independence, whereas Civil Disobedience sought only limited dominion status.
quiz.why: While Non-Cooperation was a milder tactic of withholding cooperation from governance, Civil Disobedience was an offensive strategy that deliberately broke British laws.

quiz.q: Why did Mahatma Gandhi permit armed self-defence and refuse to condemn violence during Quit India?
options: He succumbed to pressure from revolutionary socialists after losing organizational control over the Congress.
He concluded that strict adherence to non-violence had already achieved all major national goals.
He yielded to British provocations after realizing that peaceful mass satyagraha was historically premature.
He strategically viewed non-violence as a mobilization tool that was dispensable once masses joined.
quiz.why: Francis Hutchins argued that Gandhi was a strategist who used non-violence to mobilize the masses, discarding strict non-violence once mass participation was secured.
